correctness.rationale: A column contains at most one zero and at least two mutually adjacent positive vertices, so the ordinary and total outer-independent Roman feasible sets agree, not merely their minima. For z zeros and t twos, z≤n and z≤3t, giving saving z−t≤floor(2n/3). With k=ceil(n/3), the path centers have gaps two or three and endpoints within one step (the singleton path is direct). For a cycle n≥4, 2k≤n≤3k realizes the requisite two/three gaps. Properly color the centers with at most three defender rows; for a three-gap use both its different boundary rows, for a two-gap the preceding defender's row. At each center at most two row values are forbidden for its zero, including its defender row; this verifies global zero independence and domination. On C3 one two cannot defend three independent zeros, as the two neighboring columns themselves are adjacent; the listed two-zero witness attains 3m−1. At n=3q, z−t=2q and the two inequalities force z=3q and t=q, so the q defended three-column neighborhoods are disjoint and cover the columns. The path has one phase, a cycle of length at least six has three; center zeros are independently chosen off the defender row in each block (no restriction across middle-column zeros). Adjacent defender rows must differ. Path coloring multiplication and the trace of (J−I)^q for the cycle give the two claimed counts, including q=2 on the cycle. Bounded direct graph enumeration over all 3^9 labelings each of K3×P3 and K3×C3 gave (minimum,count)=(7,6) and (8,108), respectively; the second is an exceptional-case count, not a claimed formula. Frozen CHECKER.py was inspected, not run. Neither finite diagnostic is used for the general proof.
